decision.reason: The cleanup validates the receipt, candidate and control identities only before the deletion sequence, then deletes pathnames without a delete-time identity and inventory recheck. Production freshness cannot repair this immutable executor defect.

sequence: validateRuntime, validateControl, validateCandidate and validateReceipt complete
rm(receipt) executes without re-reading the receipt tuple and SHA immediately before unlink
rm(candidate,{recursive:true}) executes without re-reading the candidate root tuple, exact manifest and inventory immediately before deletion
rm(control,{recursive:true}) executes without re-reading the control root tuple, placement receipt and full inventory immediately before deletion
defect.impact: A same-path replacement after validation but before its rm can be deleted even when its inode differs. The recursive directory removals can delete a foreign replacement tree. This contradicts identity-bound cleanup and the request's substitution fail-close boundary.
defect.testGap: The fixture changes the supplied control tuple before validation. It does not replace the receipt, candidate directory or control directory after successful validation and before deletion.

requiredSuccessor: re-read and compare each target's exact dev/inode/type/nlink and signed bytes or complete inventory immediately at its deletion boundary
refuse deletion and retain the substitute when the receipt, candidate root/tree or control root/tree is replaced after initial validation
add direct adversarial fixtures for same-bytes-new-inode receipt replacement and same-inventory-new-inode candidate and control replacement after validation
preserve the old current, old release, unit, service, three listeners and five public hashes before and after every allowed mutation
force-false push a wholly-new exact request and request a wholly-new no-retry cleanup-only lease
require a separate zero-write readback before releasing the Creator emergency Heavy state
